A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MaAS research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including the additional appendix material in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original benchmark results, resource measurements, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and cross-model and cross-dataset transfer experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds Figure 10, showing operator-sampling probabilities at different sample counts.

M1.justification: The supernet, query-conditioned controller, early-exit mechanism, cost objective, and Monte Carlo/textual-gradient updates remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. Appendix B.3 documents an existing component without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, MATH, MultiArith, HumanEval, MBPP, and GAIA, with the same transfer and held-out-operator scenarios. The new sampling analysis does not introduce a dataset, task, population, or input environment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark, efficiency, and transfer comparisons. This includes the GAIA-specific AutoGPT, TapeAgent, and Sibyl comparisons and the GPTSwarm/AFlow cross-dataset comparisons.

E3.justification: New Figure 10 compares layer 1 and layer 3 sampling probabilities at labeled sample counts of 100, 200, 500, and 800. This adds a limited analysis setting; existing dataset splits, metrics, LLM configurations, and optimization settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds Figure 10 to examine how operator selection changes as sampling progresses. This extends the existing static layer-distribution and sensitivity analyses; the previous ablation questions, case studies, and transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: There is no changed disclosure of seeds, repeated experimental runs, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. Figure 7's shaded variability display and variance discussion are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes the HumanEval cost for MaAS without textual gradients from 0.09 to 0.90, in units of 10^-3 dollars. Figure 10 adds sampling-probability results across four sample counts. Benchmark, efficiency, and transfer scores in Tables 1–3 and 7–8 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, sampling equations, and gradient expressions remain substantively unchanged. Fixing an unmatched brace in Definition 3.2 is a notation correction; no new mathematical reasoning or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the claimed performance advantage from 0.54%–11.82% to 0.54%–16.89%. The new upper bound matches the unchanged MBPP scores for MaAS and MacNet in Table 1: 82.17 versus 65.28. The central methodological, efficiency, and transferability claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds the interpretation that increasing sampling helps MaAS avoid overly confident early stopping and favor testing and self-refinement in deeper layers. Existing interpretations of resource allocation, transferability, and unseen-operator selection remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 expands from acknowledgements and a pointer to code into substantial documentation of textual-gradient optimization: a meta-prompt, Python operator templates, architecture-archive input, and the required JSON output interface. The abstract also changes code availability from forthcoming to reported available. This materially expands documentation of a central component.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work categories, and positioning against automated agent design and neural architecture search remain unchanged. No substantive citation addition or revised novelty relationship is evident.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized typographic corrections, updates affiliations and correspondence details, adds publication information and acknowledgements, and expands two appendix subsections. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the four-panel Figure 10 and a boxed textual-gradient prompt/code listing. Figure 9 is repositioned to accommodate the new plot, and text and table placement shift. Existing figures and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.3 fills an important documentation gap by exposing the textual-gradient prompt and operator templates, while Figure 10 adds a useful diagnostic of sampling behavior. These improve inspectability and understanding. The new diagnostic remains lightly documented, and the core method and benchmark validation are unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
